Note::regex_findall¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note::regex_findall(std::string_view pattern) const -> TokenBatch
Note::regex_findall(std::string_view pattern, std::int64_t flags) const -> TokenBatch

What It Does¶

Finds every regex match in each text cell and returns the matches as a TokenBatch.

This is the extraction-oriented regex method. Use it when the goal is not just “does this match?” but “pull out every token that matches this pattern.”

That makes it useful for:

  • numbers

  • ticket IDs

  • dates

  • hashtags

  • symbol-like fragments

It is a token-extraction surface, not a yes/no predicate surface. If your next step depends on the matched substrings themselves, regex_findall() is the right shape.

Parameters¶

pattern

The regex pattern to apply to each text cell.

The returned tokens are the matched substrings themselves, flattened across the whole Note.

flags

Optional regex-engine flags encoded as an integer bitmask.

Use this overload only when you already know the regex-engine flag contract you need from the implementation. This page does not assign guessed semantics to unnamed flag bits.

Returns¶

TokenBatch A flattened token stream plus offsets() that mark where each original Note element begins and ends inside that stream.

Examples¶

Example 1. Extract every digit run from two text cells.

auto note = pluss::make_note({
    "Order 17 ships on 2026-08-02",
    "Ticket 204 closes at 18:30",
});

auto matches = note.regex_findall(R"(\d+)");
std::cout << "regex_findall_digits tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < matches.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << matches.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "regex_findall_digits offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : matches.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

regex_findall_digits tokens: [17] [2026] [08] [02] [204] [18] [30]
regex_findall_digits offsets: 0 4 7

Example 2. Extract only uppercase letter runs when the pattern is more structural than numeric.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"AX-17", "BY_204"});
auto matches = note.regex_findall(R"([A-Z]+)");
std::cout << "regex_findall_caps tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < matches.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << matches.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "regex_findall_caps offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : matches.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

regex_findall_caps tokens: [AX] [BY]
regex_findall_caps offsets: 0 1 2

Example 3. Extract hashtag-like fragments from short social-style text.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"#alpha update", "ship #beta now"});
auto matches = note.regex_findall(R"(#\w+)");
std::cout << "regex_findall_tags tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < matches.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << matches.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "regex_findall_tags offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : matches.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

regex_findall_tags tokens: [#alpha] [#beta]
regex_findall_tags offsets: 0 1 2

Notes¶

  • offsets() is the boundary map back to the original cells.

  • In the example above, the first input cell contributes tokens in the flat range [0, 4), and the second contributes tokens in [4, 7).

  • If you only want a boolean answer, regex_findall() is heavier than a regex predicate method because it materializes every match.

See Also¶

  • Note::contains: literal substring inspection without regex.

  • Note::split_whitespace: tokenize by whitespace rather than regex matches.
